verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Three routine rewritings, no mathematical difference. (i) The Lean states the identity in difference form R(u+w,p+pi) - R(u,p) = ... rather than R(u+w,p+pi) = R(u,p) + ...; these are the same equation in a normed vector space. (ii) The Lean writes the quadratic term as spatialDerivative e t x (e (t,x)), i.e. (w.grad)w, where the paper writes div(w (x) w); since div(w (x) w) = (w.grad)w + (div w)w and the paper's increment w is divergence-free by hypothesis, the two agree on exactly the objects the paper applies the identity to. The Lean carries no divergence-free hypothesis, so on that point it is the more general statement, but it never produces the div(w (x) w) form itself. (iii) ResidualCalculus works pointwise at a fixed (t,x) with explicit differentiability hypotheses (DifferentiableAt in time, ContDiff 2 in space for u and e, DifferentiableAt for p and q) and at viscosity exactly one, which is the viscosity of the paper's R as well (the paper's L has -Delta w with coefficient one). CorrectionStep.nonlinearResidual_add_sub is the same identity with a perturbation a already present: setting a = 0 collapses its three transport terms to transport b b, which is the paper's quadratic term.
